correctness.rationale: Three positive pairwise-transition channels reconstruct the stated polynomial system. On the strictly positive simplex, U/sqrt(X)=1/2 and Y+U-X/2=1/8 are exact invariants, giving Y=(sqrt(X)-1/2)^2/2 and sdot=-s²(1+2s)/4 for s(0)=1/10. This scalar flow stays positive, tends to zero, and satisfies t*s→4, so t²Y→8. The limiting positive components are X=1/4,U=1/4,Z=1/2; log(U(0)/U∞)=log(6/5) is the exact L1 integral. Graph arcs read directly from channels give a DAG transition graph and unique dependency cycle X↔Y, with Y having persistent successor X. The source explicitly permits a persistent successor inside the cycle (Proposition 1 Case 1). The inverse-square law logically excludes any exponential upper bound; all substantive steps analytic and replayed symbolically.
